questions_asked: At a busy US airport, roughly how many checked bags does a typical departing passenger have on average?
Of the checked bags screened, what fraction is it typical that passengers have them checked close to the gate rather than well ahead?
During a busy peak hour, how many minutes before departure do most passengers finish checking their bags?
expert_answers: Roughly 0.5–0.7 checked bags per departing passenger on average at a busy US airport — i.e., about half to two-thirds of passengers check at least one bag, and a small share check two or more. A common planning figure is around 0.6 checked bags per passenger. This is an empirical judgment, not a precise value; it varies with airline business model (legacy carriers higher, low-cost carriers lower), route type (domestic vs. international), and season.

At a busy US airport, only a small fraction — typically on the order of 5–15% — of checked bags are checked close to the gate (e.g., at the gate or a late/curbside drop shortly before departure) rather than well ahead at the main check-in counter. The large majority of checked bags are tendered at the ticket counter or curbside well before departure, so they are available for screening in the normal baggage flow. This is an empirical judgment, not a precise value; it varies with airport layout, airline policy, and how "close to the gate" is defined.

Most checked bags are tendered well before departure — typically on the order of 45–90 minutes ahead for domestic flights, and longer (2–3 hours) for international. During a busy peak hour the bulk of bags are checked at the counter or curbside in that window, with only a small late fraction arriving within roughly the last 30–45 minutes (airlines commonly cut off counter check-in about 30–45 minutes before domestic departure). This is an empirical judgment, not a precise value; it varies with airline policy, route type, and airport layout.
